newsitem.title: USA: SOCCER-COLLYMORE SCORES ON DEBUT FOR ASTON VILLA IN L.A..
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-COLLYMORE SCORES ON DEBUT FOR ASTON VILLA IN L.A..

text.p: England striker Stan Collymore scored a goal in his debut for Aston Villa as the English Premier League team drew 1-1 with the Los Angeles Galaxy in a friendly match on Wednesday.
Collymore, signed last week from Liverpool for $11.4 million, slipped by a static defence to nod home a Mark Draper cross in the 75th minute at the Rose Bowl.
Brazilian Welton had scored for the Galaxy in the 60th minute.
"It was nice to get on the scoresheet, especially since the opposition is always trying so hard to beat an English team," Collymore said afterwards.
"It was a great cross from Mark."
Collymore's new manager, Brian Little, was pleased with the performance.

"He's pleased he scored, the lads are pleased he scored. It always helps a striker to settle in. But I'm not judging anyone yet. tonight was more important for him to build relationships with his teammates," said Little.

The 26-year-old England striker, who had not played for two weeks, looked sharper in the first half and worked well with Dwight Yorke as the visitors stroked the ball around in front of a sparse 8,759-crowd in a stadium that holds nearly 100,000.
Last week, Collymore signed a four-year contract with Villa with a further one-year option to play for the team he supported as a boy.
The almost $12 million transfer fee Villa paid Liverpool is almost as much as the payroll for the entire 10 Major League Soccer teams. The league caps team salaries at $1.3 million each.
Joining his new teammates on their American tour, Collymore spent a couple of days in Las Vegas before flying to Los Angeles for Wednesday's game against last season's MLS runners-up.
Villa, who drew 1-1 with MLS's San Jose Clash last week, were playing without Andy Townsend and Steve Staunton who were both on World Cup duty with Ireland against Liechtenstein.
Also missing from the lineup was English international Gary Southgate and striker Savo Milosevic.

Early in the first half, Collymore cut in from the left and his low cross was nearly turned in to his own net by Galaxy defender Danny Pena. In the 30th minute, he took a pass from Yorke and fired a low shot from outside teh area that was well saved by goalkeeper Kevin Hartman.
The closest he came was five minutes later when he shot low from 20 yards, forcing Hartman to dive low to keep out the shot. Julian Joachim latched on to the rebound but the keeper blocked his shot.
Twice near the end of the first half, Hartman had to stretch to push the ball around the post from long-range shots by Draper.
